The climate in Kyustendil

Kyustendil is about 520 m above sea level. The warmest month is August, with an average high of 29°C; the coldest is January, when nights average −3°C. Around 730 mm of precipitation falls in a year on average, most of it in March (about 82 mm).

Kyustendil lies in the Kyustendil Valley at the foot of Osogovo, at about 500 m. The valley is sunny and sheltered, with warm summers and winters fairly mild for its altitude, which is why it is known for its cherries and other orchards. The town’s mineral springs have been used since Roman times.
